## Overview

In research one often encounters the problem that software works on one machine
but not another, or was working last year but not since a recent system update.
Containers are an effective way not only to get software *working* consistently
on different computers, but also to produce the same outputs across them.

Whilst running a container is simple, managing its entire lifecycle, and further
creating and sharing your own container images, is easier with an understanding
of the technology. In this module we introduce the fundamental concepts that
underpin the rest of the course, before getting up and running with
containers published online, using Podman Desktop.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you will:

- Appreciate the challenges of reproducible computing in research, and how
  containers offer a solution
- Understand core container concepts: images, containers, layers, runtimes and
  registries
- Run a container image from an online registry on your computer
- Know how to connect storage and system devices (e.g., GPUs) to containers
- Be confident managing the lifecycle of a container, and providing your own
  start-up commands
